reviews.reason: The numbered unit is present on printed p. 64/PDF102, but the English flattens distinct editorial layers into an unqualified botanical description. The bracketed word, parenthetical tree phrase, and bracketed cut-tree clause must not be treated as equally secure continuous Ethiopic text. Printed p. 65/PDF103 is Greek and apparatus, not an Ethiopic continuation. Its note 10 discusses, rather than resolves, the competing botanical constructions.
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace the speculative notes with an account of the printed interventions: p. 64 note 21 identifies an Ethiopic gloss; note 22 discusses the tree phrase absent from the Ethiopic translation; p. 65 note 10 explains Charles's bracketing of the cut-tree clause. Do not confidently gloss the bracketed word as 'shaded' or present shoots from a felled tree as settled. Move botanical notes away from 'middle of the earth' and remove the misleading alternative attached to 'shaded'.

reviews.reason: The printed Ethiopic supports water from the east beneath the mountain and its flow toward the north. Preserve that distinction. The facing Greek has a different directional expression and an explicitly disputed reading; it must not replace the Ethiopic silently.
reviews.suggested_text: And there I saw a holy mountain, and beneath the mountain was water from the east, with its flow toward the north.
reviews.footnote_changes: Move the note from 'holy mountain' to the water clause. Explain that 'from the east' and 'toward the north' describe different aspects of the water's course. Preserve the source asterisk at ወ*ውሕዘቱ as an editorial marker, not a lexical character.

reviews.reason: The directional phrase supports east, not northeast. The higher mountain is eastward; the deep, narrow valley lies between the mountains; water travels toward the mountain. The printed edition marks an intervention in the water clause, and p. 64 note 38 expressly associates that emendation with Greek evidence.
reviews.suggested_text: And I saw another mountain toward the east, higher than this one. Between them was a deep, narrow valley, and water flowed through it toward the mountain.
reviews.footnote_changes: Delete both northeast alternatives. Attach the height alternative, if retained, to 'higher', not to the valley's width. Attach the textual note to 'through it': this follows Charles's marked edited reading, whose apparatus cites Greek support. Do not imply that this is an unproblematic unanimous Ethiopic reading or identify the destination mountain more specifically than the text does.

reviews.reason: The unit begins at the bottom of printed p. 64/PDF102 and continues at the top of printed p. 66/PDF104 through ሠለስቲሆሙ።, before the numeral 5. Thus 'another' is immediately completed by 'mountain'; both existing notes are misleading. The candidate ወካእእት requires correction against the printed ወካልእት. The precise English force of ኑሐ remains unresolved here. The first valley is below and between the mountains; the second is explicitly deep and dry toward the extremity of the three. Do not transfer the second valley's adjectives to the first.
reviews.suggested_text: And to the west of this was another mountain, lower than it and [height or extent uncertain]. A valley lay below between them, and another deep, dry valley lay toward the extremity of the three.
reviews.footnote_changes: Delete both existing notes. The supplied repair is provisional: its English square brackets mark unresolved translation, not brackets printed in the source. Retain the unresolved demonstratives rather than assigning named modern hills or valleys. Explain the page continuation and the source-glyph correction before approving a complete replacement.

reviews.reason: Printed p. 66/PDF104 explicitly numbers this unit 5 before the XXVII heading. It describes deep valleys without breadth, hard rock, and a negative tree-planting clause—not a forest. The negative is supported by Charles's printed edited text, but apparatus note 15 says it was added in accordance with Greek; that editorial dependence must be disclosed.
reviews.suggested_text: All the valleys were deep and narrow, of hard rock, and no tree was planted on them.
reviews.footnote_changes: Add a textual note at 'no': Charles prints the negative, but p. 66 note 15 identifies it as an addition made in accordance with Greek and records differing Ethiopic evidence. Preserve the printed critical marking around the planting clause. Do not expand 'no tree was planted' into a claim about a forest or every kind of vegetation.

reviews.reason: Printed p. 66/PDF104 explicitly numbers this unit 6. It ends at ወጥቀ፡ አንከርኩ።; the XXVII heading follows immediately, before ወእምዝ፡. Therefore the material preceding that heading belongs to chapter 26 despite its storage in ch27.txt. All six numbered units are structurally accounted for, but the chapter is not editorially complete: 26:1 and 26:4 remain on hold, and the proposed repairs are unapplied.
reviews.suggested_text: And I marveled at the rocks, and I marveled at the valley, and I marveled greatly.
reviews.footnote_changes: Preserve the repeated marveling and singular 'valley'. Retain the source asterisk on the repeated verb as a critical marker; p. 66 note 18 records an omission in q. No geographical identification is warranted.
